children: Bajaj Finance has closed its qualified institutional placement (QIP), allotting 11.41 crore equity shares at ₹1,025 apiece to eligible institutional investors. The issue has raised approximately ₹11,700 crore. The floor price for the issue was fixed at ₹992.25 per share.

The non-banking financial company (NBFC) had launched the QIP to raise fresh capital from institutional investors, with the proposed issuance comprising up to 11.41 crore equity shares of face value ₹1 each.
The issue price of ₹1,025 per share represents a discount of around 5% to the prevailing market price.

Separately, the board of Bajaj Finance had approved the allotment of 5.74 crore warrants to its promoter and holding company, Bajaj Finserv, for nearly ₹5,800 crore. The warrants were allotted at an issue price of ₹1,010 apiece.
The NBFC had approved the QIP proposal in October. The capital raise is expected to strengthen its balance sheet and support business expansion amid robust credit demand in India.

According to the preliminary placement document dated November 11, the proposed QIP issuance was expected to result in a dilution of up to 1.8% of the company's pre-issue paid-up equity capital of 6,225.95 million shares.

The proceeds from the QIP will be used to repay deposits, loans, commercial papers (CPs) and non-convertible debentures (NCDs), along with interest payments on these borrowings, falling due after the allotment of equity shares. The remaining proceeds will be utilised for general corporate purposes.
The equity shares were offered to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), including resident Indian QIBs and eligible foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), subject to applicable regulatory requirements.
Morgan Stanley India, Kotak Mahindra Capital, J P Morgan India, IIFL Capital Services, JM Financial and Axis Capital were the book-running lead managers to the issue.

Bajaj Finance has continued to report strong business growth, with its assets under management (AUM) increasing 26% year-on-year in the September quarter. This marked its fastest growth since the March 2025 quarter.
Meanwhile, the company's capital adequacy ratio stood at 20.33% as of September-end, compared with 20.90% at the end of the June quarter and 21.23% a year earlier.
Bajaj Finance shares closed 0.63% lower at ₹1,110 on Monday. The stock has gained 14% so far in 2026, outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined more than 3% during the same period.

title: Bajaj Finance closes ₹11,700 crore QIP, allots shares at ₹1,025 apiece; stock in focus
